Messages.Author: Eugene Earnshaw-Whyte
Messages.Body:
First, my vote on the promo card. I think Lucita or Fatima would be the best
choices. Both have the 'cool' factor that one wants in a promo card --
particularly if you get a nice slinky picture. And both belong to clans that
I think you should release pre-constructed decks for.

Second, pre-constructed decks. These are absolutely vital: the major problem
with Jyhad/V:TES was the number of cards that one has to buy in order to
construct an acceptable deck. Make sure these are constructed so as to be
playable right out of the box, which is trickier than it sounds. I think it
would be wise to include some random cards, as well as a fixed group -- it
will make it more likely that people who get hooked will buy two starters
for their favorite clan.

The critical thing is the choice of clan. Your concern that the
preconstructed decks offer a variety of playing styles is, I think, very
appropriate. There are essentially 4 things V:TES decks do -- bleed, vote,
fight, and block Decks can focus on any of these, and it would obviously be
best if the pre-constructed decks covered the range of these types. Going
just from the basic disciplines, the clans offer the following potential:

Assamites: fight
Brujah: fight, possibly vote
Followers of Set: bleed, maybe vote (but probably not)
Gangrel: fight
Giovanni: Bleed, possibly fight
Nosferatu: Possibly fight or bleed.
Lasombra: Bleed, maybe fight or vote
Malkavian: Bleed
Ravnos: Fight, Intercept
Toreador: Bleed, Intercept, Vote, maybe fight
Tremere:Fight, Bleed, Intercept
Ventrue: Bleed, Vote

I think the wisest course would be to release at least 6 decks. Leaving
aside the Sabbat for a moment, the clans I would pick would be Brujah,
Toreador, Tremere, Ventrue, Assamites, and Giovanni. Here's my reasoning:

1 These clans are, along with the Followers of Set, probably the most active
in vampiric society generally (excluding the Sabbat) as well as being active
opponents of one another. The Nosferatu Gangrel, and Ravnos tend to stay out
of things a bit more. A game about struggles between vampire Methuselahs can
justify excluding those clans, but you could hardly justify leaving out the
Ventrue or the Tremere.

2. They offer a good mix of abilities. The Ventrue and Toreador can both
vote well, the Tremere and Toreador intercept, etc.

3. Nosferatu, Gangrel, and Ravnos are all weak clans, and it would be
difficult to put together a strong enough pre-constructed deck. This is also
something of a problem for the Assamites, but they can be fixed fairly
easily and the background recommends their inclusion.

The most likely substitution that would also work well, I think, would be
replacing the Assamites with the Followers of Set. This has the advantage of
including a stealth/bleed deck. The other advantage it has is that, as it
stands, the Followers of Set are more playable than the Assamites: the
assamites are a weak clan. The reason I think it would be better to include
the Assamites is that their weakness can easily be fixed with a couple of
well-thought out quietus cards, and Stealth/Bleed decks can be frustrating
for new players to deal with. If you want the starter decks to be balanced
against each other, it might be best to leave the Setites out.

Disciplines: If you are only releasing 4 or 6 (six would be far better)
pre-constructed decks, you'll have to decide what to do with the disciplines
that none of the clans use. If you don't make a pre-con Gangrel deck, will
you include protean cards in the boosters? What about chimerstry and
serpentis? I would recommend only releasing disciplines for the clans you're
releasing Pre-cons for --this is a MUST if you aren't putting vampires from
the other clans in the booster packs, obviously. What's the point of getting
protean cards if no-one can use them?

The Sabbat: You have two main options. You can either re-release the Sabbat,
or integrate Sabbat cards into the rerelease of V:TES. Either would be fine,
I think. Either way, you should release pre-constructed Tzimisce and
Lasombra decks. If you just re-release the Sabbat expansion, you should
still release Tzimisce and Lasombra Pre-Cons. It will make the set much more
accessible to a new player. When the expansion first came out, my V:TES
group tried to entice new players, but failed, because we had to honestly
tell them that buying a box of Sabbat boosters for a hundred dollars
(canadian) would be the absolute minimum they would need to make a playable
deck.

I think the best option of all is to release the six clans I mentioned, as
V:TES second edition, and then maybe a month later, re-release the Sabbat
with appropriate Pre-constructed decks, bringing the total up to eight.

New Cards: If you don't include the disciplines that are missing from the
Pre-con clans, and take out some of the more useless cards, you'll have a
fair amount of space for new cards. This is VERY IMPORTANT. If you don't
include new cards in V:TES, established players won't buy 'em because they
already have enough. Even a few useful cards at each rarity level, however,
are likely to hook us because we're suckers for the game. There are some
excellent card ideas available on the web, and I bet you could buy the
rights fairly cheaply, if coming up with them in-house is a problem.

If you include Assamites, you might consider printing all-new, or mostly all
new Quietus cards. Simply put, they need to be able to kill vampires more
efficiently. Also, there is the issue of whether Ancient hearts was a
limited edition run.

Something else to consider is 'Box Powers'. Some sort of power associated
with each clan that they get access to at all times. People are familiar
with the concept from other CCG's and like it. There is a perception among
people I have talked to that V:TES didn't reflect the character of the World
of Darkness sufficiently. Including more cards that deal with the
relationship between the sects would be a good idea, but so would
emphasizing the distinctiveness of the clans. Box powers would help you do
this. Here's one suggestion: The assamite box power should allow assamites
to Diablerize other vampires, and prevent any bloodhunt vote from being
called on an Assamite vampire. This would reflect the metaplot -- and it
makes no sense, in terms of the background, that Assamites should almost
always have to refrain from Diablerie becasue they are afraid they will be
burned due to their lack of political influence. This could be made a master
card, too.

You should definitely include cards that relate to the ongoing metaplot --
it's what will help hook Vampire players. There is also a lot of room for
more useful political actions: the background suggests lots of
possibilities. It's also important to clean up the rules -- and I don't
think the current FAQ should be used as is, there are numerous rulings that
are probably not best for the game.

Regards, Eugene

I don't agree that adding a box power would necessarily be THAT difficult,
although I agree that one would have to be careful to balance the powers.
Battletech is an example of a game that retrofitted box powers onto an
existing system without any particular difficulty (although they didn't put
as much thought into them as they should, they still worked fine). Box
powers are typically available from the beginning of the game, so however
they work, Clan Impersonation would probably be irrelevant. My suggestion
would be to require that 2/3ds of a Methuselahs crypt be composed of
Vampires from a clan in order to gain access to the clan's box power.

The other advantage of including box powers is that it allows W-Wolf to go
some way towards balancing the inherent strength of the clans. Some
combinations of disciplines are more effective than others, and the clans
with less effective combinations can be aided somewhat by a more effective
box power, in order to balance the preconstructed decks against each other.
This is particularly important if the pre-constructed decks are mostly or
entirely fixed. They should be balanced so that they all have an equal
chance of winning a game. Box powers can help that. They will also encourage
clan-themed decks, which is probably good.

My example box power was about the strongest I would hope any box power to
be. I consider Assamites to be among the weakest clans at the present time,
so their box power should ameliorate their weakness if they are made a
pre-con deck. Allowing them to diablerise with impunity makes perfect sense
from the viewpoint of the background, and it makes it substantially easier
for them to take out other minions. Celerity and Quietus are very weak
combat disciplines, so I think making burning minions easier for the
Assamites is worthwhile. Also gives them something to use their obfuscate
on.

Just to anticipate objections, I'm not saying that Assamites aren't good at
combat: I'm just saying that they are not as good as the competition. The
good Quietus strikes cost blood and are hard to use. It's easy for Assamites
to knock minions into Torpor (flash, Taste of death), but it isn't easy for
Assamites to burn minions or seriously knock down their pool, beacause their
cards don't stack (like potence) or do really large amounts of damage (like
Thaumaturgy. The exception being The Khabar: Honor). Assamites are also have
difficulty dealing with Strike: Combat Ends, and unlike the Tremere, lack
the Bleed Bounce and intercept to keep themselves alive until the guy runs
out of Majesty's (or whatever).

Dude, that's a FIVE CARD combo, and it costs 4 blood! And if they have a
maneuver of their own, you're totally screwed. Typical situation: assamite
finally gets the five cards required, enters combat, maneuvers to long
range.... and opponent S;CE. Now 3 of the other 4 cards are totally useless
until the assamite picks up another maneuver. I'm not saying that the cards
are awful or anything, but Thaumaturgy strikes are better and potence cards
stack. Other combat decks can do the same thing with fewer cards and for
less blood. Far too often, an Assamite will find himself with, say 2
maneuvers, 2 blurs, and a blood sweat. Or no blurs. Or no maneuvers. Or no
taste of death to finish it off. The more cards the combo needs, the less
likely you'll actually get all the right cards in your hand. Not to mention
how expensive it is to use all those blood sweats and blurs. You won't be
getting blood back on you vampires very easily unless you are using Taste of
Vitaes, and then there's another card you want, making it a six card
combo...

It's not that this won't work sometimes, but, generally, it won't work
nearly often enough (particularly because of maneuvers and S:CE). And since
Assamites don't really have intercept, bleed bounce, or significant
pool-regaining capacity, they don't usually get a whole lot of time to build
up a good hand or work through all of their opponents S:CE.

Further, Assamites also tend to get the short end of the stick when they go
up against other combat decks. An assamite's worst nightmare is a combat
deck that uses animalism, because Drawing Out the Beast makes all of their
long-range-only strikes useless. Immortal Grapples mess them up badly,
obviously. They do pretty good against Tremere, in that they can knock the
Tremere to torpor pretty consistently, but they can't actually finish the
Tremere off usually, and the blood on their minions gets worn down by theft
of vitae's until they can't fight effectively (remember how many of their
combat cards cost blood).

I think the easiest way to fix this is a Quietus pre-maneuver that adds to
the damage of all Quietus strikes. A theft-of-vitae type strike (without the
range) would also be good, since Quitus has one in the RPG (Leech). It would
be good if Quitus was made more flexible, having both short-and long-range
strikes.

They should probably also have something to help deal with S;CE. My solution
(which also deals with some other issues -- namely, the weakness of
celerity), would be to add celerity card that cancels both your own strike
and your opponents. Should probably cost 1 or 2 blood. It would serve to
give celerity a way of surviving immortal grapples, and another way of
dealing with S:CE.

Eugene

the entire primary resources (pool) vs. secondary resources (minions,
equipment, master cards etc.) argument that comes up time and time again,
but hasn't come up for ages, that I recall.

Bleed hits primary resources, so you oust them quickly. Vote hits primary
resources, so you oust them quickly. Combat hits secondary resources,
which allows you to then hit primary resources, so you oust them more
slowly. A heck of a lot more fun AND once you can get someone's vampires
killed, they can't hit back. Bleed has the risk that, whilst you're
bleeding someone oust, because they still have their vampires, they might
be able to get you. Combat takes its time removing that risk, albeit at

Fair enough, but given the potential re-release of the game, it seems like
as good a time as any to look again at old rulings, based on whether or not
they're best for the game. Appealing to a ruling by the designer is
appropriate for settling disputes in play, but it's pretty much irrelevant
to settling a dispute about what the design of a game SHOULD BE.

This dispute is not about what the rules are. This dispute is about what the
rules should be. Insofar as we on this list might have some small influence
on any changes that might be made to the game, we should consider what rules
would be best for the game, in terms of improving balance, fun, clarity,
etc.

I don't actually have a strong opinion about whether or not first strike
should beat dodge: I lean towards thinking it would be best if it did, as

Now I don't follow your logic here. Even if we did change First
Strike to resolving before S:CE and Dodge, it would have very little
impact...except to _possibly_ make equipment based combat a little more
risky. Let's take a look at the cards that give First Strike and I'll
show you why.

Canine Horde, Fast Hands, Blessing of Durga Syn and Shattering Blow all
only affect weapons and equipment. How often do you see equipment and
weapons used in tournament decks? Not all that often. In fact, decks
that make extensive use of equipment are few and far between. As a
result, these cards don't get used all that often. Making them resolve
before S:CE and Dodge is unlikely to have any real effect since the
reason they don't get used now isn't likely to change.

Silence of Death gives Assamites First Strike for hand and melee
strikes. However, Assamites can't send someone to torpor using
hand or melee strikes unless they are out of blood or are equipped with
the Sengir Dagger or Kali's Fang, both of which are unique. What about
Blood Agony? It gives Assamites agg hand damage...but not until the
2nd round of comabt. By then the the S:CE has already hit the table.

Back Stab is the only card that allows a vampire to have First Strike
without limiting the strike. However, it requires Celerity and costs
two blood, a steep price, and the vampire must be blocking. First off,
intercept combat is a strategy that's generally doomed to failure (as
discussed in another thread) and the only vampires that can
consistently be able to block and can use this card are the Toreador nd
!Toreador. They're not the first clans to come to mind when I think of
clans that are dangerous in combat. Assamite, !Gangrel and Brujah
decks, because of lack of intercept ability, are almost always more
pro-active and are not likely to use the card at all.

Muddles is the only serious use of First Strike, striking with 4 hand
damage. However, that's all he can do without more equipment. Being
an Ally and a unique one to boot, he's vulnerable to a multitude of
cards and since he only has one life, all it takes is someone to block
him or rush him with damage prevention, ranged damage or just more than
4 blood.

In the past, one of the arguments has been, "What if WotC comes out
with a card that makes First Strike more abusable?" Well, with LSJ on
board and with the attitude that WW is taking towards the game, I think
that we're more likely to see a higher quality product that we did with
WotC. I'm not expecting a Protean or Potence card that gives First
Strike hand strikes for 1 blood any time soon.

Strike resovle first. I'd like to repost a post I made over a year ago

Now I realize that defensive cards are supposed to be cheaper than
offensive cards. However, I found the disparity quite excessive.

Let's see if I can tackle this issue. Readers be warned. This post
may take a while and is likely to be about as intersting to read as
Bills of Congress from 1872.

To begin with, please note the fact that while the original VTES book
does say, "A "dodge"...prevents the effect of the opponent's strike
that round, even if the opponent's strike was delivered with First
Strike," there was no such statement in the Jyhad rulebook. And as
has been pointed out in the past, there were many problems in the
translation from Jyhad to VTES. However, both books do say, "The damage
inflicted by a minion with First Strike is resolved before the strike
of the opposing minion begins," and can be used as a basis to declare
that First Strike _does_ happen before S:CE and Dodges.

When I examined the cards that gave First Strike and Dodge, I examined
them based on effect and opportunity cost. The cost of opportunity can
be summed up by the following factors: Inf./Sup. Discipline
Requirement, Blood Cost, Restrictions of Usage, and Additional
Benefits. I found that the cost of opportunity of First Strike was
much higher (almost 3 times as much) than the cost of opportunity of
Dodges. The fact that a Dodge can cancel most of the strikes that you
may get from a First Strike leads me to believe that there is a serious
game balance issue...esp. when you consider that _any_ minion can use
Dodge and very few minions can use First Strike.

Restrictions of Usage includes the following: DNR (do not replace until
combat has ended), Equip (requires the opposing minion to have
equipment), Weapon (requires equipment to be a weapon), Close (must be

And the actual useful defenses against frisbees are: Obedience,
Elysium, S:CE, Drawing out the Beast. Since Lids provide a press,
you'd better be packing a ton of prevention to survive. Maneuvering
back to close range is a joke - the maneuvers available and naturally
included in a thrown-stuff deck (Gate, Flash, Rush) will pretty much
ensure it never gets caught. Not to mention Pursuit - better than
Flash in this sort of deck since you can cycle it as a free strike to
save a Blur/blood. The only other long range strikes out there worth
a damn are the Assamites and Tremere, and if it's not THA/CEL, the
Tremere will die. The Assamites have their own problems.

>Compare with the defenses against Immortal Grapple/Blur: Obedience,
>Elysium, damage prevention, fight back with your own short range *hand*
>strikes, maneuver to long range. Pretty similar situation, except the IG
>strategy is probably more card efficient, which is why I don't think a
>Celerity anti-S:CE card gives the Brujah anything they don't already have.

Again, damage prevention is going to be difficult against a good IG
deck, since IG gives a press. Fighting back is a little easier since
some clans and vamps have ways to make their hand strikes nasty, and
maneuvering away from them is a lot easier since IG decks include
fewer maneuvers. The card efficiency is much the same either way:

Rush, Gate, Blur, Lid, Lid - 8 for POT/CEL
Rush, Signpost, IG, Blur, Taste - 9 for POT/CEL
Rush, Signpost, IG, Undead Strength, Taste - 5 for POT

five cards each. Taste is necessary at close range since otherwise
your guys may die. The reason IG decks work and frisbee decks don't
is directly attributable to the ability of the IG deck to prevent S:CE
from ever being played. Psyche! is functional, but wasteful of cards.

>> that it would provide a REDUNDANCY to IG. A lot of our wallpaper
>> cards are there because they're redundant [snip]

>isn't a reason not to print it. On the other hand, to the Tories, the
>Assamites, and the Gangrel-Antitribu, such a card is not wallpaper at all,

No, NOT exactly your point. It WOULD be useful, but it would not
provide an ADVANTAGE over IG. The Brujah need no help - let us not
waste our time helping them excessively. The Gangrel-Anti need a lot
more help than just an anti-S:CE card, and the Toreador don't rank
-that- high on my list of "need combat help" clans. One card to
Auspex and one card to Quietus would cover things nicely (since Harika
Guljan is a laugher with only QUI.)

Messages.Author: Eugene Earnshaw-Whyte

The proposal was not for a card that cancels all strikes for a combat. That
WOULD be silly. The proposal was for a card that would be played sometime
around strike resolution, and cancel both your strike and the opponent's
strike. Probably cost about 1 blood. This would be useful for a few things:

1. Dealing with S:CE. Assamites and Toreador trying combat would be
thankful.

2. Dealing with being Immortal Grappled. As a defence, you could cancel both
your strike and your opponent's.

3. Allowing potence/celerity to stand some chance against potence/fortitude.

Note that this would not prevent additional strikes from being played, nor
presses continuing the combat (thus granting both people more strikes).

How would this card make celerity decks 'unstoppable'?Celerity by itself
does worthless damage. Imagine a fight between a celerity deck a a potence
deck. Potence plays Torn signpost, Immortal grapples. Celerity cancels both
strikes, blurs. Net result: both minions have played two cards, lost 2
blood, and potence has a press. Unbalanced? I think not.

In my gaming group we rarely see potence celerity rush decks because
fortitude/potence (or Thaumaturgy!)works so much better. Celerity is, in my
opinion, one of the weaker disciplines in the game, despite the number of
cards it has. This card would just make it a bit more worthwhile.

>generally you DO know what's in your opponents decks. I know my friends
>decks almost as well as I know my own.

Mostly, though, a lot of the balance of the game has to be considered
*in* tournament settings. Individual groups can do many different
things to balance the game one way or another. One of the most
difficult is social pressure - something that the NJL seems to use
extensively to limit the playing of Return to Innocence (since people
such as Noal have noted that the card is rarely seen but there is good
natured joshing when the card *is* played). Another way is the one you
also have - that decks settle into routines.

Also, if you know your friends decks well, there is an argument to be
had about whether that is the most effective thing anyway, for playing,
but also what if they change their deck?

Let us say that I generally play Clan Hypothetical, and I want to use
their box power. Fine. Everyone knows this. I come along, I show the
bits of my deck necessary and then everything goes on as before. What
about when I change my deck? If I *don't* claim the box power, you have
an immediate (if slight) advantage, in knowing how my deck has changed.
And if I claim a *different* box power, you know even more. And if I
don't claim the box power, my deck would be sub-optimal, quite possibly
- if, say, I can't claim the bonus stealth that Clan Hypothetical gets
on its political actions, I am hampering myself.

>> Indeed not. One of the best defences against bleed is a strong offence -

unable to play (effectively) your Undead Strength and Taste of Vitae. A

>> Indeed. But all the damage in the world is not going to help against Skin
>> of Steel. All the areas have holes to be exploited. If you don't cover
>> the bases well enough, you don't get to do your stuff. Cover them too
>> well, the deck becomes less focused. You choose where you draw your line.

there are many other fortitude cards to pick from - skin of steel is one
of the better examples, but multiple Skin of Rocks are also popular.

>>

>knocking
>> > Arika into torpor before she bleeds you to death. Celerity is acceptable
>as

>> That's what its supposed to be.
>
>I disagree. I think that disciplines can't (shouldn't) be designed to be
>primarily secondary. That might be what they get used as, but that shouldn't
>be the design.

I note the use of the word "shouldn't". I can see a strong case for, if
you were designing the game from the ground up, making each discipline
intrinsically as playable as any other, on its own. However, I would
contend that this isn't what was done.

If we look through Celerity, there are a good number of cards providing
many and various abilities. I posit that none of them are particularly
effective on their own, save for combat defence - and whilst combat
defence is a powerful skill to have, all the surviving in the world
won't help your deck if it sticks around to do nothing.

For instance, Celerity has access to maneuvers (as a first examples).
Maneuvers are good combat defence, as those people like PDB6 and Josh
Duffin have explored in the past, but in terms of offence, they're
lacking. You can make sure you stay at close range, yes, but then what
do you do? Hit for hands? Similarly, and most closely related, are
presses. It would seem that in the original design, Strike: Combat Ends
was not foreseen as the powerful force it is, and certainly not in the
abusive quantities it is often seen. So, assuming that you got to the
press phase, you could press. But what could you do next round?
Exchange hand strikes for one? Strike: Dodge is combat defence again
(with caveats as noted above). Additional strikes, with primarily or
mono-celerity, are similarly poor - at inferior, you pay 1 blood to do 1
more damage - just exchanging hands again.

Celerity *thrives* on being matched up with something else. Something
else has to do the hitting out - be that Potence (Brujah), a gun, a
flamethrower, Quietus (Assamites), Thaumaturgy (Mages on Speed), Protean
(City Gangrel) and so forth.

>> > I strongly feel that celerity should be
>> > given a card that allows it to survive being immortal grappled, at the
>very
>> > least.
>>

>> supposed to do. Why *not* give Quituetus a bleed bounce card that allows
>> it to sruvive being bled, at the very least?
>

>outside the scope of celerity.

That *very* much depends on how define your card to "survive" being
immortal grappled.

However, one of the very good things about Jyhad is the strive for a
cycle of balance between different strategies. If one strategy starts
really hitting out at you, counter with alternate strategies e.g. if
Wynn-combat really starts killing you, try and counter it with a
banishment in your political deck, say. My bugbear is with the couple
of disciplines, primarily Dominate (though I can see an argument for
Fortitude too, certainly one or two facets), which do too much.

Celerity is a superb combat defence discipline, if you want it to be.
But if it can survive everything in combat, why play anything else?
Fortitude starts to play second fiddle. Fortitude is an excellent
combat defence discipline too - but in very different ways to Celerity.
Celerity tries to avoid the strike in the first place - maneuvering to
range, or dodging it. Fortitude cares not for your ability to strike
it, but simply makes that strike do no damage. So, Celerity has a big
problem with Immortal Grapple - Fortitude does not. Fortitude just
soaks up the damage. However, Celerity can survive being hit with
multiple theft of vitaes, which Fortitude cannot.

intermeshing, overlapping skill. It shouldn't be able to do everything.

Open Grate is a counter-strategy i.e. you put it in to press to end
combat, in the event that someone else plays a second round combat deck,
or your trap goes wrong etc.

Obfuscate can be a highly pro-active discipline, or at least support
your proactive attacks.

>> Therei s more to Obfuscate than just stealth.
>
>No argument. But the most effective uses of obfuscate I have seen,
>generally, have been using the stealth it provides to make important actions
>succeed. This can't come as a shock to you.

No, indeed not. Obfuscate is a highly powerful stealth discipline.
However, the Assamites *can* benefit from its other abilities, too, and
also its stealth. If you are using Bum's Rush, a Swallowed by the Night
(or similar) makes an effective way of guaranteeing the rush on the
vampire *you* want, with the maneuver (especially useful for some clans,
of course). The idea of adding a little stealth to rushes has long been
seen to be a useful possibility, especially in decks which utilise
single vampires highly. If I can only rush you once or twice a turn, I
need to target my rushes a lot more effectively than if I have 5 weenies
to rush you with. That's partly why Wynn's +1 stealth (D) rush is so
highly prized - you get to pick the problem, and then deal with it,
unless they can get intercept.

If you want to get a Kali's Fang out, say, you could also use obfuscate
to equip it - either a couple of stealth cards here and there, or a
disguised weapon.

Since you need to oust your prey, a few stealth cards will add to a few
computer hackings to expedite their demise.

And so on.

If you play CEL/QUI combat *and only CEL/QUI combat* with the Assamites,
no, Obfuscate won't do much for you - but the Presence on the Brujah
won't do much for a CEL/POT deck, either. If you alter your deck, you
can exploit a highly useful skill, with many rewards.

somehow) and maneuvers are easily countered by ranged damage, among other
things. A combat deck that has gotten lazy and skimped on maneuvers and
ranged damage can be succesfully defended against. Defence using celerity,

> intermeshing, overlapping skill. It shouldn't be able to do everything.

I agree entirely. But some disciplines are stronger than others, and this is
a gamebalance issue that can be addressed without making the weak
disciplines (like Celerity) 'do everything'. I'm not suggesting that
Celerity start to bounce bleeds, or prevent damage, or even give stealth. I
think it should be able to do moderately more damage, and have stronger
defense. In other words, it should be able to do what it already does, just
a bit better.

bloodhunt. That's all.

IME, the Toreadors don't do all *that* well, though on paper they might.

They lack the low capacity princes of the Brujah to exploit voting,
don't have a Ventrue Headquarters or any natty cards to really help them
vote - something that they really should do, since they often form
keepers of the Elysium and members of the Harpies, and so forth. Their
princes are hampered by slightly sub-optimal discipline mixes, too -
look at Tatiana, for instance. :( Not, for my money, a great prince -
she has AUS, when she would really benefit from PRE. Sure, she has +1
bleed, but that's not good for the vote side of things. Rake makes a
much better prince, with PRE and a Praxis.

compared with weenie Dominate bleed, they only have 1 action modifier,

hands). It provides great defence at superior, giving them the ability
to gain pool, but it has problems hitting out fast and hard, IME.
However, I've never really seen anyone try and do a weenie Toreador PRE
Aire of Elation/Misdirection feast, which I think could work really
rather well, especially with a couple of hunting ground type cards
around (maybe even a Gird Minions if you can get the PRE for Social
Charm/Legal Manipulations).

intercept with guns. It looks like it should be possible on paper, but
it really isn't that easy to pull off, because of the vulnerabilities of
guns. I'd love to see it done properly.

of Adonis, to discourage people from failing their votes, but nothing to
proactively help them pass it which other clans don't already have
access to.

also that damage from blood of acid isn't a strike, so it can't be prevented
with the jacket.

send the Tzimisce to torpor, but the Brujah is taking agg, so he goes
down -- and then the Tzimisce can play Taste of Vitae. This obviously works

deflected/countered, the small ones get ignored. If the bruise and bleeder

> currently. Improving it will toss the game out of balance - therefore

Improving it will definitely not toss the game out of balance, if it is done
carefully. Only a few additions are required. The most pressing is a method
by which a deck that relies on celerity for defence can survive being
immortal grappled. Before people bring up 'celerity should never be caught
at close range', I would like to again mention Drawing out the Beast:
Potence/Animalism is a common discipline pairing. Shadow step also defeats
Celerity's vaunted ability to maneuver. Another addition I feel would be
valuable is a card that, while being expensive, gives +1 hand damage at
advanced. While potence or Thaumaturgy would still be much stronger in
combination, it would allow celerity by itself to be moderately effective in
combat. The assamites can use the help. the Brujah wouldn't care, and it
would be fun to see a Toreador trying combat. Toreador can't bleed as well
as Seites or Makavians, can't vote as well as Ventrue. Adding a bit more
potential for combat to celerity might make them actually use the
discipline, rather than being basically Auspex/Presence machines.

but, like I said, difficult to employ properly. It's hard to get the right
balance for how many to put in the deck (judging from my attempts at
constructing assamite decks). Tends to take up space in your hand, or else
not be around when you actually want it. And many of your good minions don't
have advanced obfuscate, which makes the card worthless, essentially. And,
since assamites go through blood quickly, often your minions won't have
enough blood to play it. That's what I meant by 'difficult to employ'.

And in your example, Cardano probably uses obedience on Melek (or Anson uses
majesty, or Crusher kicks his sorry ass), and then Tansu Bekker gets blocked
with a second tradition domain. At least, that seems more representative of
what I'd be likely to actually see in play. :-)

And, yes, it is one of the few actions Assamites can perform (along with
Arson and Bum's rush) that obfuscate is quite useful at getting through
succesfully.

Mm-hmm. That used to happen to me all the time. I admit, getting a Tzimisce

cards, it's easy to have an unfocused deck that does nothing well.

> superior to stop dodges.

Fair enough. My group tends towards larger minions than is standard, I
think.

.
>
> Donal and Constanza are useful to ANY Brujah deck, as they come with a
> Prince title, a special ability, and POT/CEL. The Dominate is a

> tossing around Carthage Remembered. It's worth it to lose Volker
> sometimes.

Considering you're paying 3 cost more than Volker in order to gain advanced
potence and a moderately useful power, it doesn't seem like the best deal,
to me. But then, I'm a bit biased because I keep multiple decks constructed
at once, and generally I find my 2nd-and-fifth traditions can be used in
other decks that don't have to use substandard minions just to gain the
prince title.

> >>
> >Improving it will definitely not toss the game out of balance, if it is
done

method
> >by which a deck that relies on celerity for defence can survive being

caught
>

> don't see it doesn't mean the rest of us haven't ALREADY.

I've seen PRE/CEL plenty. Played it myself. And, I admit, the celerity is
moderately more useful than just putting in fake-outs and dodges. But, only
moderately.

A defense against IG shouldn't be a get-out-of jail-free card. It should
save you from one strike in one round. The vampire is hardly out of the
woods yet, particularly since IG gives a press and sets range to close next
round...

I don't find toreador bleed decks to be espescially powerful. They don't
have much stealth to get through, and IG + the rulings about multiple
actions really hamper their ability to get through with majesty. And they
can't fight well either. Can't Fight + Can't get through makes for a sad
deck.

Not that they're helpless, (misdirections are a godsend) they just aren't
'monsters', so far as I've noticed. And giving them a card along the lines
of the one suggested wouldn't change that, it would just make them less
pitifully helpless against potence (or, god forbid, POT?ANI. Shudder.)

>
> >at close range', I would like to again mention Drawing out the Beast:
> >Potence/Animalism is a common discipline pairing. Shadow step also
defeats
>
> Not THAT common, because the vamps end up being too big to make it
> work. It also falls over brutally and suddenly to any clan that can
> provide its own hand damage, and you had BETTER torporize them on the
> first strike or a CEL deck will eat you alive with Blur and the free

I believe the deck that one the Portsmouth Tournament just this (last?) week
was Pot/Ani. And there's a 5 pool minion (Nigel the Shunned) with POT/ANI. I
see the combination all the time (slight exaggeration).

> >valuable is a card that, while being expensive, gives +1 hand damage at
> >advanced. While potence or Thaumaturgy would still be much stronger in
> >combination, it would allow celerity by itself to be moderately effective
in
> >combat. The assamites can use the help. the Brujah wouldn't care, and it
>
> The Assamites need the help given to their OTHER strikes, not their
> hand damage. Why have QUI when you're just going to be a CEL hand
> damage machine?

That they do. I envision this proposed card as being weaker at advanced then
fists of death at basic, so if the Assamites were given some more useful
Quietus strikes, they wouldn't have to rely on it, but it would remain a
potentially valuable option. AT best, with a blur, you'll be doing six
damage while losing 3-4 blood if the opponent strikes just with hand, so it
won't really be the most efficient combat mechanism.

>
> The Brujah would be helped - there are a lot of pot/CEL vampires out
> there who need skill cards to be fearsome. This would make them
> worthwhile out of the gate.

Pot cel doesn't need skill card to be fearsome (torn signpost/blur does 6
damage). CEL/pot should still be more effective than just the CEL by itself.

> nobody plays with Aire of Elation in your group?

Uh, no, pretty much all of us use the card. Particularly when we're playing
Toreador.

>Toreador bleed
> -very- well. Nothing bleeds as well as Malkavians, obviously.

Setites can, pretty much (except for problems with the disciplines on their
minions)

>Why do
> you want a clan who is second-best at two of the basic styles to be
> any good at ALL at the third? This isn't unbalancing? If the Malks
> had any -good- way to save their butts in combat, it would be VERY
> broken. Right now, they pretty much are soft mooshy bags to be
> smacked around by any combat deck nearby.

2nd best? Malkavians, Setites, Giovanni, Lasombra, and Ventrue all bleed
better than Toreador. Brujah can bleed almost as well, and Tremere aren't
particularly far behind (if they're trying). They bleed better than the
clans that lack dementation, presence, and dominate. That isn't saying all
that much. Heck, even Gangrel can bleed better than Toreador, if they use
dominate.

They might be second best at voting, but only if you don't count all the
voting decks that don't rely on a particular clan.

Adding the potential to fight to the Toreador doesn't strike me as
unbalancing. The more combat cards they put in, the less well they'll
bleed/vote/do other stuff. It just gives them the potential to be slightly
more well-rounded if they want -- which seems good, since they don't really
specialise at anything.

Eugene

> fleshcrafts with Tzimisce. The people you want to bonecraft
> IG you, and the rest majesty, with the result that they sit

I would tend to agree with this. Bonecraft and Fleshcraft, while
amusing cards, don't tend to be all that useful.

> Carrion crows, aid from bats, blood of acid, body arsenal,
> horrid form and possibly drawing out the beast, song of
> serenity, and scorpion sting, are the core combat cards for
> Tzimisce, in my opinion. And IG is more risky against Tzimisce

I'd say it's more risky against the Gangrel. They're more likely to
prevent the damage and pop claws on a Scorpion Sting. The only good
thing about Blood of Acid is that, like IG, it is played before strikes
are chosen, but after range is determined to be close. So it does make
a good response card.

Personally, I've not gotten around to Tzmisce combat since my
"Transformers" deck using Bauble and more Ghoul Retainers, Assault
Rifles and Flamethrowers than god.

> Considering you're paying 3 cost more than Volker in order to
> gain advanced potence and a moderately useful power, it doesn't
> seem like the best deal, to me.

I tend to agree. Donal and Costanza never go in my Brujah political
decks for two reasons. They're over 6 cap and they don't have Presence.
In political decks, I find it's better to use smaller vampires so you
can get things going much faster.

What I did find a good use for them was a Lasombra/Giovanni/Brujah
DOM/POT deck that was fairly vicious.

> A defense against IG shouldn't be a get-out-of jail-free card.
> It should save you from one strike in one round. The vampire
> is hardly out of the woods yet, particularly since IG gives a
> press and sets range to close next round...

As noted above, IG may only be played after range has been deterrmined
to be close. If combat is at long range, IG may not be played and you
will get no press from it. If you want to count on having a press, pack
Trap or Mighty Grapple.

> I don't find toreador bleed decks to be espescially powerful.
> They don't have much stealth to get through,

They don't need it. A Toreador bleed deck isn't going to use large cap
vampires. All they need to do is come at you en masse and use S:CE for
the vampires that get blocked.

Bernie had a variation on that theme using multiple Aching Beauty/Change
of Target where he'd bleed you with Social Charm. If you blocked, you
lost the pool from the Aching Beauty cards and never got a shot at him
because Change of Target cancels combat altogether. If you didn't
block, he layed down Aire of Elation. Using Flash/Majesty kept the
occasional IG deck from ruining his day.

> Setites can, pretty much (except for problems with the
> disciplines on their minions)

While I agree 100%, liberal use of discipline cards does help.

>> you want a clan who is second-best at two of the basic styles
>> to be any good at ALL at the third? This isn't unbalancing? If
>> the Malks had any -good- way to save their butts in combat, it
>> would be VERY broken. Right now, they pretty much are soft
>> mooshy bags to be smacked around by any combat deck nearby.

Uh...my OOC Malk deck had even the IG decks running for cover. I'd pack
Obedience to deal with rush combat until the end of my predator's minion
phase and then lay waste to a vampire that annoyed me with White
Phosphorous Grenade/Rotschreck and then play Graverobbing to steal it.
And occasionally, just for fun, I'd use Malkavian Time Auction to give
the player a chance to buy it back. In terms of keeping my predator off
of my back and still be able to work over my prey, it was one of the
most highly successful decks I've ever made.

> 2nd best? Malkavians, Setites, Giovanni, Lasombra, and
> Ventrue all bleed better than Toreador.

Giovanni?!? They have a _horrible_ discipline spread. They also don't
have the small cap vampires that can pull off the mass assault the
Toreador can. Same goes for the Lasombra. Setites suffer a little as
well. Malkavian and Ventrue, I'll grant you since, being Camarilla,
they have access to a lot more small cap vampires.

> Heck, even Gangrel can bleed better than Toreador, if they use
> dominate.

Since they don't have Dominate as a common discipline, this is a
pointless observation. A PRO/DOM deck is not a Gangrel deck.

While you are, of course, entitled to your belief that the Toreador is a
substandard clan, my fairly extensive experience does not bear this out.

Messages.Author: Eugene Earnshaw-Whyte
Messages.Body:
>But if the people you want to bonecraft IG you, and the rest Majesty,
>they'll just do the same with these, especially Aid from Bats. And if
>the rest are just Majestying anyway....

Since you can't be immortal grappled at long range, it is less of a problem
for me -- and Blood of Acid, like I said, makes a very nice counter if they
actually catch me.

A deck can majesty against these -- but that isn't actually a huge problem,
because your cards cycle through your hands either way. And aid from
bats/carrion crows are free, so it doesn't really cost you anything to play
them, as long as you have plenty in the deck. Ideally (and this actually
does happen fairly often) the cards you cycle in combat (whether or not they
accomplish anything) allow you to pick up more blocking cards, which
promptly cycle, and by then you have some more combat cards...

It's a defeasible strategy (Theft of Vitae's are a problem, actually), but
it deals very well with POT, and tends to come out ahead against POT/CEL in
my experience. You just have to rely more on scorpion stings than aid from
bats against POT/CEL, is all.

> well. Malkavian and Ventrue, I'll grant you since, being Camarilla,

They aren't going to do a weenie minion bleed, if that's what your thinking,
but those decks tend to be multi-clan anyhow.

The giovanni discipline spread sucks for fighting, but it works fine for
bleeding. I direct your attention to Gloria Giovanni, a 4 pool minion who
can bleed for 6 at +1 stealth, or for 4 at +2 stealth. Stefano, Carlotta,
and Enzo also make excellent bleeders. The primary advantage of Giovanni as
bleeders, however, is that Whispers from the Dead, together with Carlotta
Giovanni, make them essentially immune to hand clog. Whatever card they
currently lack can easily be procured by Rudolpho Giovanni as a +1 stealth
action.

>
> > Heck, even Gangrel can bleed better than Toreador, if they use
> > dominate.
>

> Since they don't have Dominate as a common discipline, this is a
> pointless observation. A PRO/DOM deck is not a Gangrel deck.
>

Dominate isn't a clan discipline, but it is moderately common among Gangrel.
Stanislava, Iliana, Faruq, and Ingrid Rossler all have it. One of the decks
I regularly see is Gangrel with dominate. It is designed so that it is very
effective with only basic dominate on a minion -- and Stanislava is truly
fearsome.

> While you are, of course, entitled to your belief that the Toreador is a
> substandard clan, my fairly extensive experience does not bear this out.
>
> Noal

I never said that the Toreador are substandard. Nosferatu, Assamites are
substandard. Toreador have a good discipline, an average discipline, and a
weak discipline, so one would expect them to be kind of middle of the pack.
Their large selection of vampires, and the general excellent quality of
those vampires improves them somewhat. I said that they weren't
exceptionally good at anything, and (more importantly) that Celerity is
virtually useless to them. I further maintained that making them somewhat
more capable in combat would not make them unstoppable, or even unusually
good.

If we follow a general policy of making all the weak disciplines better
(much easier than trying to make the strong disciplines weak), along with
improving the vampire selection for those clans which are currently
shortchanged, we shall find that, miraculously, all the clans will be on a
much more even footing. Any improvement in Celerity should be accompanied by
a corresponding improvement to all the weakest disciplines. I've discussed
Celerity mostly because I think I have a pretty good idea of what needs to
be changed. A discipline like animalism is tougher.

Eugene
